author: Raul Trey Lopez
title: Bexar County man accused of trying to entice person he believed was 16-year-old girl online - NewsBreak
text:
By Raul Trey Lopez ,
4 hours ago James Kenneth Rogers is charged with online solicitation of a minor and possession of mushrooms after investigators say he spent weeks communicating with an undercover officer posing as a 16-year-old girl. (Bexar County Sheriff's Office ) A weekslong undercover investigation targeting online child predators ended Wednesday with the arrest of a Bexar County man accused of trying to lure what he believed was a 16-year-old girl to his home for sex, the Bexar County Sheriff's Office said.
James Kenneth Rogers II, 45, was booked into the Bexar County Jail on charges of online solicitation of a minor. Deputies also charged him with possession of a controlled substance after finding illegal mushrooms during his arrest.
Sheriff Javier Salazar said the investigation began June 1 after the U.S. Secret Service alerted the sheriff's office that Rogers had been communicating online with someone he believed was a 16-year-old girl.
Instead, investigators said, Rogers had been messaging an undercover officer posing as the teenager.
Over the following weeks, Rogers allegedly convinced the undercover officer to move their conversations from the Whisper app to text messages before repeatedly inviting the person he believed was a 16-year-old girl to his home for sexual activity, Salazar said.
Although Rogers never traveled to meet the person he believed was a minor, investigators said they had enough evidence to establish the elements of the offense. Deputies with the Human Exploitation Unit obtained an arrest warrant before taking Rogers into custody Wednesday.
Rogers was arrested at his home without incident.
Salazar said Rogers has no known prior arrests involving online solicitation of a minor, though he did not immediately have information about any other criminal history.
Salazar said the case serves as a reminder that children can be targeted through virtually any online platform.
In this investigation, the conversations began on the Whisper app before moving to text messages.
"But that's not to say that just because your child's not on that particular app that your child is 100% safe," Salazar said. "We've found these cases on every single app."
Salazar said online predators also use gaming platforms and other internet-connected services to contact children.
The investigation was conducted by the Bexar County Sheriff's Office Human Exploitation Unit in partnership with the U.S. Secret Service.
"Anytime a child is on a device that has a connection to the outside world, they are absolutely vulnerable to being approached by someone that has bad intentions toward them," Salazar said.
